title: Compak® Sporting: the compact format
summary: Compak® Sporting appeared at the end of the 20th century as a compact form of Sporting™: less land, faster shooting and easier for spectators.

body.html: A full Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ course needs a lot of land: woods, hills and several layouts. Many clubs do not have that. So the idea came up to bring the variety of sporting targets onto a small plot.

This is how Compak® Sporting began. Its rules state that the discipline was created in 1989 and adopted by FITASC in 1991, so it is a format of the late 20th century. It spread quickly: FITASC has held European Championships since 1995 and World Championships since 2004.

The idea is one field. A Compak field has 6 traps lettered A to F and 5 shooting stations in a line. The targets fly over a marked rectangle in front of the shooters. They go in many directions, as in Sporting™, but all on one field.

The format has several advantages. A club needs less land and fewer traps. Shooting moves faster. And spectators can see the whole squad (the group of shooters who shoot a round together) and all the targets from one spot, so Compak® Sporting works well on video.
The name and the rules of Compak® Sporting are a trade mark registered and protected by FITASC. That is why we write the ® sign and do not invent other versions of the name.

Today Compak® Sporting is often a beginner's first discipline. It is easier to find near home, and its skills carry over to a full Sporting™ course. How a Compak field works in detail: How a Compak® Sporting layout works.

key_points.html: Compak® Sporting is a compact form of sporting on one field.
The rules say it was created in 1989 and adopted by FITASC in 1991.
One field: 6 traps lettered A to F and 5 shooting stations in a line.
The name and the rules are a trade mark of FITASC.

did_you_know.html: In Compak® Sporting a spectator can stay in one place and see all the targets of a round. On a full Sporting™ course that is not possible.
